seo_title: Why Contractor Reviews Decide More Than Price
title: Why Reviews Decide More Than Price
content:
###  **The Threshold Effect** 

BrightLocal's survey of more than a thousand United States adults found that 91 percent read local reviews, and that most will not consider a business rated below four stars. 

That second finding matters more than the first. It describes a threshold rather than a preference. Below a certain rating, a company is not competing on price or service — it is not being considered at all. 

###  **Where This Sits in the Decision** 

Reviews function as a filter early in the process. A homeowner assembling a short list uses ratings to decide who makes it. Only after that does anything else — price, availability, responsiveness — come into play. 

Which means review management is not a marketing tactic layered on top of everything else. It is a prerequisite for the rest of it working at all. 

###  **The Limit of What Reviews Do** 

Reviews decide who gets considered. They do not decide who gets called. 

Several strong companies in the same market will clear the four-star threshold on the same short list. At that point the homeowner is choosing among options that all look acceptable, and the tiebreaker is usually something else entirely — a neighbor's recommendation, a truck they have seen on the street, a name they simply recognize. 

###  **The Practical Sequence** 

Get above four stars and keep reviews current, because below that nothing else matters. Then build the recognition that decides which of several qualified companies actually receives the call. 

Companies that do only the first are on the list. Companies that do both get contacted.
